claims: The Bohr Hamiltonian with a gamma-stable potential V(gamma) = c/(4B beta^2) * (gamma - gamma_e)^2 generalizes the PRM beyond rigid rotor assumptions.
Under the adiabatic approximation, the total energy separates into an exact 1D harmonic oscillator gamma-vibrational term A' n_gamma' and rotational eigenvalues B' r_s^I.
Gamma-vibrational excitations (n_gamma' = 1, 2) on a single particle-hole configuration generate a new class of MchiD with identical rotational patterns and in-band B(E2)/B(M1) transitions.
Coupling a single high-j particle to a gamma-stable core generates multiple rotation-wobbling doublets with strong collective E2 inter-band transitions.

Interband E2 enhancement alone does not uniquely confirm wobbling, as gamma-vibrational core-particle coupling naturally yields B(E2)out/B(E2)in ~ 0.3-0.8; multi-phonon spacing and S(I) staggering indices are required to discriminate.
